brief: Goldman Sachs Research raised its December Brent forecast to $90 from $85 and projects Brent averaging $80 in 2027, arguing Persian Gulf exports have rebounded close to 2025 levels since late September. Over the same weekend, Goldman's futures desk (Quinn) reported hedge funds buying Brent call options, triggered by Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iran disrupting shipments inside the Gulf: Managed Money and other accounts bought $4.9bn in futures as Brent gained 5.1% during Oct 6-13, with 32% of Managed Money's new long exposure built through call initiations. That buying cheapened the 3-month put-call skew and lifted 5-delta call implied vol relative to 50-delta, leaving dealers "incrementally shorter gamma," a setup that could amplify a price spike if tensions worsen, though tail pricing stays far below February's peak and speculative net length (~$14bn) stays far below April's ~$38bn peak. The Dec-Jan curve spread still declined despite the buying, which the desk attributes to undetected "dark" tanker flows transiting the Gulf, the same flows Goldman's bearish 2027 case depends on, even as Goldman's own oil risk premium estimate grew from $22 to $25 in a week.
